name: Apple Companion Link
description: Apple peer-to-peer companion and Continuity-related service discovery. Instance names and TXT data may be privacy-preserving or activity-specific; this record alone does not identify a particular feature or prove a connection is active.

name: Apple Remote Pairing
description: Apple RemotePairing discovery used by supported iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS devices for trusted network pairing and related device communication. TXT fields may contain opaque identifiers and authentication tags, not friendly device names.

name: Apple QUIC-related service (unclassified)
description: Observed in this network capture as UUID-named UDP endpoints on Apple devices. The name suggests a QUIC-related transport, but its precise application purpose is not publicly documented; use the SRV target, port, and packet conversations as evidence rather than inferring a user-visible service.

name: Google Chromecast / Cast
description: Google Cast receiver discovery. Cast clients may also query application-specific DNS-SD subtypes beneath _sub._googlecast._tcp to filter discovery results by receiver-app criteria. Opaque subtype labels (including percent-escaped or binary-looking values) are selectors, not standalone device identifiers, and cannot be mapped to an app name from the label alone. Correlate subtype PTRs with the base _googlecast._tcp PTR and the receiver's SRV/TXT records to identify the device.
r1: Use Chromecast predefined option if present; otherwise Other

name: SFTP over SSH
description: Secure File Transfer Protocol service over SSH. It may be advertised alongside _ssh._tcp; confirm the TXT data and endpoint before treating both as separate services.

name: Apple Sleep Proxy
description: Apple Bonjour Sleep Proxy advertisement used to help sleeping network devices remain discoverable and wake on demand. Its presence is infrastructure signaling, not a user session.

name: Printer PDL Data Stream
description: Direct printer Page Description Language data-stream service, commonly associated with TCP port 9100. The advertised SRV port is authoritative; seeing the service does not mean a print job is in progress.

name: Scanner Discovery (eSCL / AirScan)
description: Universal eSCL/AirScan scanner discovery over TCP. Inspect SRV and TXT fields for the device model, capabilities, and advertised endpoint; this is discovery metadata, not evidence of a scan in progress.

name: Network Scanner Discovery
description: A scanner or multifunction printer advertises network scanning discovery. The device name, port, and TXT fields can identify the vendor and model; the record alone does not prove that scanning is active. Protocols and port usage vary by manufacturer (for example, Canon network scanners may advertise BJNP/MFNP details).

name: Secure Scanner Discovery (eSCL / AirScan)
description: Secure eSCL/AirScan scanner discovery over TLS. Check the advertised target, port, and TXT capabilities; compare with _uscan._tcp for any non-TLS endpoint. Presence alone does not indicate a scan is underway.

name: Matter (commissioning/discovery)
description: Matter service discovery; confirm exact service advertised by device

name: Spotify Connect
description: Spotify Connect / ZeroConf discovery for a hardware device or software endpoint that exposes Spotify Connect. Spotify's published ZeroConf discovery uses this DNS-SD type and advertises an HTTP endpoint; its TXT record can include CPath, the path to the ZeroConf API. A service instance identifies the endpoint, not necessarily the physical product or current playback state; inspect instance, SRV, and TXT data.

name: Sonos speaker discovery
description: Sonos-related local speaker/system discovery. This service type is a useful Sonos product fingerprint, but it does not by itself name the speaker model, prove playback is active, or describe every Sonos control path. Correlate the instance, target, SRV/TXT data, and other evidence; Sonos discovery can also involve SSDP/UPnP and other advertised services.
